question: Evaluate $\int \sqrt{\cot x} dx$.
explanation:
Let $t=\sqrt{\cot x}$ so $\cot x=t^2$.

Differentiating gives $-\csc^2x\,dx=2t\,dt$.

Thus $dx=-\frac{2t}{1+t^4}dt$.

Substitute into the integral to obtain $-2\int \frac{t^2}{1+t^4}dt$.

Evaluating using standard integrals gives the final result.

options.A: $-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\cot x-1}{\sqrt{2\cot x}}\right) - \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \ln\left|\frac{\cot x-\sqrt{2\cot x}+1}{\cot x+\sqrt{2\cot x}+1}\right| + C$
options.B: $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\cot x-1}{\sqrt{2\cot x}}\right) - \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \ln\left|\frac{\cot x-\sqrt{2\cot x}+1}{\cot x+\sqrt{2\cot x}+1}\right| + C$
options.C: $-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\cot x+1}{\sqrt{2\cot x}}\right) - \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \ln\left|\frac{\cot x-\sqrt{2\cot x}+1}{\cot x+\sqrt{2\cot x}+1}\right| + C$
